title: 4.7 Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)
description: Types, transmission, symptoms, prevention, and treatment of STIs including HIV/AIDS, gonorrhea, syphilis, chlamydia, HPV, herpes, and trichomoniasis

questions.question: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) spread primarily through:
questions.explanation: Sexually transmitted infections are infections which spread through sexual contact.

questions.question: Which of the following is among the most common STIs in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Trichomoniasis, syphilis, gonorrhea, chancroid, and HIV/AIDS are the common STIs in Ethiopia.

questions.question: Trichomoniasis is caused by which type of organism?
questions.explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by the flagellated protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis.

questions.question: A common symptom of trichomoniasis in infected women is:
options: Yellowish discharge and sore itchy vagina
questions.correctAnswer: Yellowish discharge and sore itchy vagina
questions.explanation: Some infected women have a yellowish discharge and a sore, itchy vagina.

questions.question: Chlamydia is caused by:
questions.explanation: Chlamydia is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis, which are small bacteria.

questions.question: What symptom do most infected men with chlamydia experience?
options: Clear or yellow discharge from the penis
questions.correctAnswer: Clear or yellow discharge from the penis
questions.explanation: Most infected men have a clear or yellow discharge from the penis.

questions.question: Left untreated, chlamydia can lead to:
questions.explanation: Left untreated, a chlamydia infection can scar the reproductive tract and lead to infertility in both sexes.

questions.question: Chlamydia can be passed from mother to child during birth, causing:
options: Pneumonia and conjunctivitis in the newborn
questions.correctAnswer: Pneumonia and conjunctivitis in the newborn
questions.explanation: Chlamydia can be passed from a mother to child during birth, causing pneumonia and conjunctivitis in the newborn.

questions.question: Gonorrhea is caused by the bacterium:
questions.explanation: Gonorrhea is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

questions.question: In men, symptoms of gonorrhea usually develop within:
questions.explanation: Men usually develop symptoms within one week of becoming infected with gonorrhea.

questions.question: Which of the following is a symptom of gonorrhea in men?
options: Yellow pus oozing from the penis
questions.correctAnswer: Yellow pus oozing from the penis
questions.explanation: In men, yellow pus oozes from the penis and urination becomes frequent and painful.

questions.question: Syphilis is caused by which type of organism?
questions.explanation: Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum, a spiral-shaped bacterium.

questions.question: If syphilis is left untreated, it can eventually damage the:
questions.explanation: If untreated, syphilis can become systemic, damaging the liver, bones, and eventually the brain.

questions.question: HIV stands for:
questions.explanation: HIV stands for Human Immunodeficiency Virus, which kills immune cells in the body.

questions.question: HIV can be transmitted through all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: HIV spreads through blood or body fluids via sexual contact, contaminated needles, blood transfusion, and from mother to child, but not through casual contact.

questions.question: Early symptoms of AIDS may include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Early symptoms include swollen lymph nodes, loss of appetite, weight loss, fever, rashes, night sweats, and fatigue.

questions.question: The first symptoms of AIDS may not appear for as many as:
questions.explanation: The first symptoms of AIDS may not appear for as many as ten years after a person is infected.

questions.question: A person who has HIV antibodies in their blood is said to be:
questions.explanation: If HIV antibodies are present, the person is said to be HIV positive.

questions.question: Which of the following is a viral STI for which there is currently no cure?
questions.explanation: HIV is viral, and there are no drugs to cure viral STIs. Antibiotics are not effective against viruses.

questions.question: Bacterial STIs such as syphilis and gonorrhea can be treated with:
questions.explanation: STIs caused by bacteria, such as syphilis and gonorrhea, can be treated with antibiotics if recognized early.

questions.question: The best way to avoid sexually transmitted infections is:
options: Avoiding sexual intercourse with an infected person
questions.correctAnswer: Avoiding sexual intercourse with an infected person
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid STIs is to avoid having sexual intercourse with an infected person.

questions.question: Which barrier method can greatly reduce the risk of catching STIs?
questions.explanation: The risk of catching an STI can be greatly reduced if a condom (male or female) is used, as it acts as a barrier.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an effective way to control the spread of STIs?
options: Seeking immediate treatment if infection is suspected
questions.explanation: Effective control includes condom use, faithfulness to one partner, seeking treatment, and ensuring partners are also treated.

questions.question: Antibiotics are not effective against which type of STI?
questions.explanation: HIV is viral, so antibiotics are not effective. Only bacterial and protozoan STIs can be treated with antibiotics.
